s.g: Used as a tag question, to emphasise what goes before or to request that the listener express an opinion about what has been said.
ex: These hot dogs are pretty good, eh?

s.g: In isolation, a request for repetition or clarification of what has just been said.
ex: —I've been studying Graphiurus murinus. —Eh? Studying what?

s.g: In isolation, expressing surprise or confusion.
ex: —You're going to be a dad! —Eh? You're joking!

s.g: An interjection used to ascertain the continued attention of someone addressed by the speaker.
ex: I went to the restaurant, eh, but my friends didn't show up.

s.g: Hey, oi; said to get someone's attention.
A greeting between friends (typically male) or display of approval.
Used to negate the following verb; (am/are/is/do/does) not.

tt: Eh? When did it start raining? I didn't notice at all.
어, 비가 언제부터 왔냐, 전혀 몰랐네.
